name: s8_d_thesis
title: The readers carry structure but a warm-start habit keeps it unsaid
caption: Both readers' outputs carry position-in-text state (decodable from the text alone at random read points inside code strings, exp 27), but only language-like properties get stated (the judge's verdict on free readouts; exps 27 and 29). Along the NLA's own RL run the structural states rate stays flat while reconstruction (FVE, inside a Python string) rises (exp 29), and a 400-step supervised adapter makes it name the state (a fixed-statement match) without costing reconstruction, correct when it names (exp 30): the gate is the warm-start register, not the reward or the reader's capacity. The readers capture position-in-text state and do not say it.

notes: Terms: 'stated' is the judge's verdict (exp 27 blind judge, exp 29 states judge); 'names' in exp 30 is the readout containing the row's fixed statement of either value. 'correct' in exp 30 is conditional on the adapter naming the state (held-out clusters, n = 32 per row); transfer to held-out rows and random points is weak (exp 30 P2-P4 failed). Text-only warm start (TextNLA) names more (0.17-0.49), which is why the gate is attributed to the warm-start register.
